solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Minister of religion caught out, having cut verse

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught is dropped from the minister

parts.note: a cleric is a minister of religion
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A clergyman, caught out, chops a poem short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes the final C from CLERIC, leaving CLERI.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a four-line comic poem about a person, a particular form of light verse.

clue.text: Like one with pride leaving home to make money in Africa

indicators.note: leaving says the letters for home go out of the lion-like word

parts.note: leonine means lion-like, and a lion lives in a pride
in means at home

explanation.surface: A proud lion-like person leaves home to earn a living in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like vanity but is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: The leone is the currency unit of Sierra Leone, a West African country.

clue.text: Ace regiment in special display for sporting event

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a special display, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A crack regiment parades at a sporting occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of horse racing at a course is a classic sporting event.

clue.text: Put outside haunt moved quickly, no longer a softie

indicators.note: the word for moved quickly is placed around the word for haunt

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so hared is moved quickly
a den is a favourite haunt

explanation.surface: Someone flees a haunted spot and toughens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hardened has become tough, so is no longer soft-hearted.

clue.text: Why ration soup so absurdly? A question in the pub

indicators.note: absurdly says the four words are rearranged into nonsense order

explanation.surface: Someone complains about stingy soup portions.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a jocular bartender's or friend's way of asking what drink you would like.

clue.text: Engineer is terrible when brought before court

indicators.note: the terrible word is placed before the court abbreviation

parts.note: dire means terrible

explanation.surface: A dreadful engineer ends up in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' is a verb here: to bring about, arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a plan is to manage or steer it, which is to direct it.

clue.text: Bold lad finally coming with a token of love

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of lad

parts.note: a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: A bold young man finally arrives with an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and bold are synonyms for adventurous and brave.

clue.text: Final message — one delivered in acceptable accent?

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the accent abbreviation

parts.note: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard accent of British English; received means accepted
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A last message spoken in a posh accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest in peace, abbreviated, is the final message on a gravestone.

clue.text: Prisoner, silly idiot getting on noon train

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: silly says the letters of idiot are jumbled

explanation.surface: A convict, a foolish idiot, boards the midday train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' turns IDIOT into DITIO. 'train' is a verb, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To condition someone is to train them to behave a certain way.

clue.text: Agree as one opposing scoundrel

parts.note: a con is an argument or person against, as in pros and cons
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Two opponents, one a rogue, agree.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a synonym of agree.

clue.text: A protein is extractable from this poison

indicators.note: the letters can be extracted and rearranged from the phrase given

explanation.surface: A scientist notes that a protein can be extracted from a toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid found in deadly nightshade, so a poison.

clue.text: Maybe a man will carry this light

indicators.note: the phrase is said to carry the answer within its letters, across the word breaks

parts.note: a heavy timber or girder that a workman might shoulder

explanation.surface: A man might be carrying a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a cryptic hint at a heavy timber, but the letters sit inside 'mayBE A Man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft or ray of light is a beam, as from a torch or lighthouse.

clue.text: Film-maker starts to seem excited, enthralled by genius

indicators.note: held captive inside the genius's name

parts.note: Einstein is a byword for genius

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of seem and excited

explanation.surface: A director seems thrilled to be in the company of a genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet director of Battleship Potemkin.

clue.text: A constraint wrecked deal

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A restriction wrecks a business agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A transaction is a business deal or exchange.

clue.text: Eager lot moved by close friend

indicators.note: moved says the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A keen crowd is touched by a dear friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego can mean an intimate, trusted companion, literally a second self.

clue.text: Troubling us with details leads to lethargy

indicators.note: troubling stirs up the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Pestering people with minutiae makes them weary.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental weariness, the same as lethargy.

clue.text: Keen OT king, first to emerge

indicators.note: the first letter of the king's name leaves

parts.note: David was a king of Israel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An Old Testament king is eager to come out first.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, the same as keen.

clue.text: A fine American, inwardly depressed, gets divine inspiration

indicators.note: the word for depressed goes inside the letters before it

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
US means American
flat means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A fine American, secretly glum, receives a heavenly spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflatus is a creative impulse thought to be breathed in from a divine source.

clue.text: Drink making one agitated mostly

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: astir means in a state of excitement or commotion

explanation.surface: A drink that leaves one mostly agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so a drink.

clue.text: Stopping in the race, but joining again?

definitions.meaning: a horse stopping at a fence in a race is said to be balking

explanation.surface: A runner pulls up mid-race but then rejoins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that halts at a jump refuses it; fusing again is re-fusing.

clue.text: Passionate daughter trapped in a fissure

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is caught inside the other letters

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: An emotional daughter is stuck in a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means fervent, full of passion.

clue.text: One provides water for diner — awful binger that's tucked into chicken?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are tucked inside the bird

parts.note: a chicken is a fowl

indicators.note: awful says the letters of binger are messed up

explanation.surface: A greedy binger tucks into chicken at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at gluttony; the definition is a table accessory for rinsing fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger bowl holds water for diners to rinse their fingers at table.

clue.text: Fellow in place of worship, English learner getting put off

indicators.note: the English learner is ejected from the building

parts.note: a chapel is a place of worship
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A man at church, an English student, is discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Scot showing some Caledonian gusto

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Scotsman shows a little Scottish enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a traditional Scottish man's name, so it stands for a Scot.

clue.text: Girl not so unmerciful

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A girl is not so cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means without pity, merciless.

clue.text: Fashionable joint

definitions.meaning: the ball-and-socket joint at the top of the leg

explanation.surface: A trendy club.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip means trendy, and the hip is the joint between thigh and pelvis.

clue.text: Stuff offered by fine grammar school

parts.note: fine means thin, as in a fine thread

explanation.surface: Material provided by a good selective school.
explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a selective state secondary school in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff in the sense of belongings or miscellaneous objects means things.

clue.text: Backward-looking newspaper boss, see, is an autocrat

indicators.note: the editor abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A reactionary editor is a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power, a tyrant or autocrat.

clue.text: One boy about to go to the head for snooping

indicators.note: about turns the word for boy back to front

parts.note: a son is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland, as in coastal place names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: A lad is about to be sent to the headteacher for prying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a promontory, not a headteacher: NESS, as in Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiness is prying curiosity, the noun for snooping.
